CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act of conduct against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of the victim's self from violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
19. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

Article 21
(1) Protection services for Women and Children from acts of violence can be implemented by UPTD PPA.
(2) As long as UPTD PPA has not been established, the duties and functions of protection services for Women and Children from acts of violence shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus and related Institutions in an integrated and sustainable manner.
(3) Protection Services as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delegated by UPTD PPA to other service units through networking and cooperation.
(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be set forth in the form of a cooperation agreement.

Article 22
Further provisions regarding the implementation of services for women victims and children involved in acts of violence as referred to in Article 19 shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 12
(1) The Shelter House as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1) provides a temporary place and/or shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.
(2) The organization and/or management of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the relevant Regional Apparatus.
(3) For security purposes and upon request of women victims of violence and children involved in acts of violence, the manager or organizer of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) may place the person concerned in a certain place that is kept confidential.
(4) Further provisions regarding the organizer of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act of conduct against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of the victim's self from violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
19. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life.

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

NUMBER 2 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SAMBAS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

CHAPTER XI
FINANCING

Financing for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children and acts of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.
Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare.
What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of women and children" is all best actions for women and children carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so that the best interests of women and children must be the primary consideration.
Letter e What is meant by "empowerment" is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act of conduct against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of the victim's self from violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
19. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 28
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children and acts of violence.
(2) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of Protection of Women and Children and acts of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.
(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
(5) Regional Apparatus shall report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of Protection for Women Victims and Children involved in acts of violence.

Article 13
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:
a. implement the policy on the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence as determined by the Central Government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating a budget for the implementation of the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity.
(3) In the implementation of the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the implementation of the responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 5
Sexual violence as referred to in Article 2 letter c in the form of: a. acts of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations in an improper or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

(3) Protection Services as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delegated by UPTD PPA to other service units through networking and cooperation.

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act of conduct against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of the victim's self from violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
19. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life.

Article 21
(1) Protection services for Women and Children from acts of violence can be implemented by UPTD PPA.
(2) As long as UPTD PPA has not been established, the duties and functions of protection services for Women and Children from acts of violence shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus and related Institutions in an integrated and sustainable manner.
(3) Protection Services as referred to in paragraph (1) may be delegated by UPTD PPA to other service units through networking and cooperation.
(4) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be set forth in the form of a cooperation agreement.

Article 13
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:
a. implement the policy on the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence as determined by the Central Government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating a budget for the implementation of the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity.
(3) In the implementation of the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the implementation of the responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

Article 3
Physical violence as referred to in Article 2 letter a constitutes all forms of acts that result in:
a. the victim falling ill or being seriously injured;
b. the death of the victim; and/or
c. causing illness or impediment to carrying out occupational work or livelihood or daily activities.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act of conduct against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.

13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.

15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SAMBAS REGENCY
NUMBER 2 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

Article 13
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:
a. implement the policy on the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence as determined by the Central Government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating a budget for the implementation of the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity.
(3) In the implementation of the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the implementation of the responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

CONCERNING

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

I. GENERAL
To prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children, the state and society are obligated to implement prevention, protection, and action against perpetrators in accordance with the philosophy of Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The state holds the view that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children, constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as forms of discrimination.

Such a view is based on the provisions of Article 28 of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. Article 28G paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to protection of self, family, honor, dignity, and property under his/her control, and shall have the right to a sense of security and protection from the threat of fear to do or not do something which is a human right". Article 28H paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia stipulates that "Every person shall have the right to receive facilities and special treatment to obtain equal opportunities and benefits in order to achieve equality and justice".

Current developments show that acts of violence against Women and Children physically, psychologically, sexually, and through neglect do in fact occur, thus requiring adequate legal instruments to eliminate violence against Women and Children.

The Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is therefore obligated to comply with these provisions. Likewise, in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.

In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women, it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and the next generation are creatures created by Almighty God, and therefore must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

The Regional Government also has the obligation to prevent, protect victims, and take action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children. For this purpose, the Regional Government requires regional regulations that can be used as instruments to realize prevention, protection and action against perpetrators of violence against Women and Children.

(4) Further provisions regarding the organizer of the Shelter House as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 12

Letter g What is meant by "the right to social rehabilitation" includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name and citizenship.

Article 8
Other violence as referred to in Article 2 letter f includes:
a. any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, either with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and/or
b. a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.
Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare.
What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of women and children" is all best actions for women and children carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so that the best interests of women and children must be the primary consideration.
Letter e What is meant by "empowerment" is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER XI
FINANCING
Article 29
Financing for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children and acts of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other legal and non-binding sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to:
a. implement the policy on the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence as determined by the Central Government;
b. establish policies, programs, and activities for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
c. cooperate with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, as well as educational institutions, health institutions, hospitals, and various non-governmental organizations concerned with Women and Children in the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(2) The Regional Government is responsible for:
a. providing support for facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence; and
b. allocating a budget for the implementation of the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence in accordance with regional financial capacity.
(3) In the implementation of the obligations of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) and the implementation of the responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government shall prepare a Regional Action Plan for the Protection of Women and Children from acts of violence.
(4) Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan for the protection of Women and Children from acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 28
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of Protection of Women and Children and acts of violence.
(2) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of Protection of Women and Children and acts of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.
(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
(5) Regional Apparatus shall report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of Protection for Women Victims and Children involved in acts of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Sambas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sambas.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of Sambas Regency.
5. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Violence against Women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against Children is any act that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
9. Domestic violence is any act of conduct against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy, integrated for the strengthening and recovery of the victim's self from violence.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
16. Shelter House is a shelter for the safety and security of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their child, or father and his child, or mother and her child or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward.
18. Household is husband, wife, and child, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care, guardianship, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
19. Society is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
20. Social rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable a person to be able to carry out social functions properly in community life.
